post.caption: Thimble once meant a thumb cover. Its Old English ancestor was built on the word for thumb. The b came in later, since the old word had none. In medieval England, most thimbles were imported, many from Nuremberg. John Lofting opened a thimble mill in London in the late 1600s. A thimble found in Wales is engraved lyke stil and love ever. Museum Wales suggests thimbles may have been romantic gifts. Thimbles were often gifts, which is why many fancy ones survive. Porcelain thimbles followed in the 1700s, with Meissen the most sought after. The Met in New York still keeps a silver thimble from 1577.
